creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Anything a person needs to do to their windows, tabs and panes should be doable from inside Muster - a menu item, a chord, or a plain `muster` verb. Not a shell trick, not an environment variable, not a config file edit followed by a relaunch, and not somebody who knows the codebase.

> ideally we dont need arcane commands or agents' helps or scripts to make this sort of stuff doable. Muster should natively make it easy and provide good UX in general

The menu is already reasonable - New Window, New Tab, the four splits, Rename Pane, Close Pane, Zoom, Find, Show Agents, Reload Configuration. This is not a request to build a UI from nothing. It is about the things that fall outside it, each of which needed something arcane on 2026-09-01.

## What one day of ordinary use actually required

| Wanted | What it took |
|---|---|
| A second window that is its own workspace | A separate `MUSTER_HOME`, a hand-written `config.toml`, and a launcher script |
| Reopen a window after closing it | `open -n`, because clicking Muster activates the running instance instead |
| Move a pane into a tab of its own | Three CLI commands and a throwaway shell (`a_2IXGSgZi7`) |
| Stop showing a machine for the afternoon | Editing `config.toml` and relaunching - `muster reload` refuses daemon changes (`a_2I6h18OU6`) |
| Recover panes after a network change | Killing orphaned processes over ssh, then relaunching (`a_2IQsToWVW`, `a_2IRcMjFs0`) |
| Find out what was wrong | Reading `~/Library/Logs/muster/*.jsonl` by hand |
| See what every window is showing | Refused; `muster window` cannot answer with two open (`a_2IZE3PiGe`) |

Several of those have cards already. What this one is for is the standard they should be measured against, and the gaps with no card yet:

- **No way back to a window you closed.** New Window makes a fresh one; nothing reopens the last, and nothing lists what is open. With two instances running, launching Muster activates whichever is frontmost rather than the one wanted.
- **No way to attach or detach a machine while running.** It is a config edit plus a relaunch, which costs every pane in the window.
- **No Close Tab.** Close Pane exists; emptying a tab a pane at a time is the only route.

## The diagnostics gap is the sharpest one

`Problem` already exists - a key, a severity, a detail, mirrored into the window from the core. The machinery is there. It is what reached the person that failed.

Every failure today printed something technically accurate and told nobody what to do. The dead panes read:

    muster-bridge: could not attach to pane w4:p2: terminal attach failed: terminal
    term_65a6bff3dab3da already has an attached client; retry with --takeover
    Process exited. Press any key to close the terminal.

True, and useless without knowing that a previous Muster's client is still holding the terminal on the far machine. The way out - kill three processes over ssh, then relaunch - was not derivable from anything on screen.

Meanwhile the run log is written to the project's own standard, with impact and remedy on the same line:

    "impact": "every pane on this daemon is rendering what it last showed, and its
               agent states are a guess about the present"
    "check":  "whether the host is reachable - the connection is being retried and
               recovers on its own once it is"

That is exactly what the person needed and it went into a file they will never open. `bridge.attach.failed` does not even manage it there - it carries an impact ("this window stays empty for as long as it is open") and no remedy at all.

So the ask is narrow: the conditions that leave a window unusable should become `Problem`s with a stated way out, rather than raw stderr in a terminal that has exited.

## What good looks like

- A window with dead panes says why, and offers the thing that fixes it, rather than showing the bridge's stderr.
- Every arrangement verb has a menu item or a chord, and the CLI is the same set of verbs rather than a larger one.
- Nothing requires an environment variable or a file edit to reach. If a setting is worth having, it is worth a way to reach it while running.
- The docs stop being the place workarounds live. `docs/cli/limits.md` currently documents several of the rows above as limits, which is honest and is not the same as them being acceptable.

## How to tell it is working

Not a test. The measure is another day of ordinary use where nothing needs a shell, a script, or somebody who has read the source - and the failures that do happen say what to do about them.
title: 🧭 Everything should be reachable from inside Muster, without shell tricks
